pinterest.title: Name Change After Marriage in Australia: The Step by Step Order
pinterest.description: A name change after marriage in Australia does not happen on its own: you update each record yourself. As at November 2026, NSW sets out the order: get your official marriage certificate from the registry (not the ceremonial one), update your driver licence and Medicare, then change your name everywhere else. NSW, Victoria and Queensland let you take your spouse's surname with your official certificate if you married in Australia. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: Your Name Change After Marriage Checklist, in the Right Order

pinterest.title: Name Change After a Destination Wedding: Passport and Paperwork
pinterest.description: Marrying overseas changes the name change paperwork. As at November 2026, NSW and Victoria say you will need to apply for a change of name after an overseas marriage. The Australian Passport Office says you can keep using your current passport after a marriage-related change of family name, and recommends booking travel in the name in your passport. Any document not in English must be translated in full. Read the full guide.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Does marriage change your name automatically in Australia? No. Signing the register changes nothing on your licence, passport or bank account. In Queensland's words, you need to contact each organisation.

Changing is a choice, and it is not only for one partner. If you married in Australia, NSW, Victoria and Queensland all let you take your spouse's surname using your official marriage certificate, without a formal change of name (as at November 2026). Victoria and Queensland say both partners can hyphenate.

The order, following NSW:
1. Get the official marriage certificate from the registry. The ceremonial certificate signed on the day is not accepted. Your celebrant can apply for it on your behalf.
2. Update your driver licence and Medicare card.
3. Use your certificate, new licence and new Medicare card as proof almost everywhere else.

Honeymoon straight after? The Australian Passport Office says you can choose to get a new passport or keep using your current one after a marriage-related change of family name, and recommends booking travel in the name in your passport.

Married overseas? NSW and Victoria say you will need to apply for a change of name. The Passport Office needs any document not in English translated in full by an accredited translator.

Our new guide covers each step, what each state says and how to go back to your previous name.
